Believing Joseph dead on seeing the coat, Jacob mourns (37:33-34).
Joseph goes to Shechem because Jacob sends him (37:13-14).
The hatred over the favoured son and his coat (37:4) is the motive the plot acts on, and the coat is stripped in 37:23.
With Joseph gone, the brothers need a story for Jacob and fake his death with the coat (37:31).
The sale removes Joseph from the pit, so Reuben finds it empty (37:29).
Judah's proposal to sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites (37:26-27) leads to the sale (37:28), though who sells is ambiguous.
The brothers follow Reuben's compromise of the pit instead of killing (37:22-24).
The dream is the motive the brothers name ('we shall see what will become of his dreams', 37:8, 19-20), months before the plot; seeing Joseph come (v18) is the trigger.
The second dream, rebuked by Jacob, deepens their jealousy (37:11) and is the motive they name when they plot (37:19-20); it makes the plot possible without forcing it.

systems.name: Sale of a person
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Slavery and the sale of persons by traders was common in the ancient Near East. Twenty shekels of silver is a young male slave's price in Lev 27:5 and in Mesopotamian records of the period.
rules_and_mechanics: Traders buy and carry people along caravan routes.
A price is paid in silver by weight.
The buyer holds the person as property.

systems.name: Symbolic dream
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Across the ancient Near East dreams were read as messages from the gods about the dreamer's future, and were interpreted by family or experts. Here the dreams carry no explicit divine speech.
rules_and_mechanics: A dream is told and interpreted by those who hear it.
The dream's images stand for people and their relations.
The text does not say that God sent it; later chapters treat the dreams as true.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Jacob tears his clothes, wears sackcloth, and refuses all comfort from his children.
system_instances.significance_note: Shows the cost of the brothers' lie and Jacob's grief, which lasts until he learns Joseph lives (Gen 45).

system_instances.outcome_summary: Reuben finds the pit empty and tears his clothes.
system_instances.significance_note: Shows that Reuben did not know of the sale and that his plan to rescue Joseph failed.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Joseph is drawn from the pit and sold to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver.
system_instances.significance_note: The turn that takes Joseph out of Canaan and into Egypt.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The Midianites sell Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar.
system_instances.significance_note: Starts Joseph's service in Potiphar's house, told in Gen 39.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Joseph tells his brothers he dreamed their sheaves bowed to his; they answer 'Will you reign over us?' and hate him more.
system_instances.significance_note: First of two dreams of rule; the motive the brothers name when they plot (37:19-20). Fulfilled when they bow to Joseph in Egypt (Gen 42-44).

system_instances.outcome_summary: Joseph tells of the sun, moon and eleven stars bowing to him; Jacob rebukes him but keeps the matter in mind, and the brothers are jealous.
system_instances.significance_note: Extends the rule over the parents; Jacob's silence leaves the dream standing for later chapters.

edges.description: The brothers send the bloodied coat to Jacob so that he will think a beast killed Joseph.
The brothers see their father's favour and hate Joseph.
On seeing him from afar, the brothers plan to kill Joseph.
The brothers strip Joseph of his coat and throw him into an empty pit.
Jacob's sons and daughters rise to comfort him, but he refuses.
Israel loves Joseph more than all his sons and makes him a long coat.
Jacob rebukes Joseph for the dream that his parents would bow to him.
Jacob sends Joseph from the valley of Hebron to see how his brothers and the flock are.
Joseph brings their bad report to their father.
Judah persuades his brothers to sell Joseph rather than kill him.
The man tells Joseph the brothers have left for Dothan.
The Midianite traders draw Joseph up and sell him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver.
The Midianites sell Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar.
Reuben rescues Joseph from their hands and has them throw him into the pit instead of killing him.
